stem: In the Gospel of Luke (4:16–21), Jesus stands up in the synagogue at Nazareth, reads "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me," and says, "This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears." Which prophet's book is he handed?
options: the book of Isaiah
the book of Jeremiah
the book of Ezekiel
the book of Malachi
why: Luke 4:17 says he was handed "the book of the prophet Esaias" (Isaiah) and read from what is now Isaiah 61:1–2, about good news to the poor and release to the captives.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (4:16–21), Jesús se pone de pie en la sinagoga de Nazaret, lee "El Espíritu del Señor está sobre mí" y dice: "Hoy se ha cumplido esta Escritura delante de ustedes". ¿Qué libro profético le entregan?
options: el libro de Isaías
el libro de Jeremías
el libro de Ezequiel
el libro de Malaquías
es.why: Lucas 4:17 dice que le entregaron "el libro del profeta Isaías", y leyó lo que hoy es Isaías 61:1–2, sobre la buena noticia a los pobres y la libertad a los cautivos.

stem: In the Gospel of Luke (17:11–19), Jesus heals ten men with leprosy on his way to Jerusalem. Only one of them turns back to give thanks. Who does Luke say that man was?
options: a Roman centurion's servant
a Samaritan, a foreigner
a priest from the temple
a tax collector of Jericho
why: Luke 17:16–18: the one who returned, fell at Jesus's feet and gave thanks "was a Samaritan," and Jesus asks whether none returned to give glory to God "save this stranger."

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (17:11–19), Jesús sana a diez hombres con lepra camino a Jerusalén. Solo uno vuelve para dar las gracias. ¿Quién dice Lucas que era ese hombre?
options: el siervo de un centurión romano
un samaritano, un extranjero
un sacerdote del templo
un cobrador de impuestos de Jericó
es.why: Lucas 17:16–18: el que volvió, se postró a los pies de Jesús y le dio gracias "era samaritano", y Jesús pregunta si no hubo quien volviera a dar gloria a Dios "sino este extranjero".

stem: In the Gospel of Luke (10:25–37), a lawyer asks Jesus, "Who is my neighbour?" Jesus answers with the parable of the Good Samaritan. What question does Jesus put to the lawyer at the end?
options: which of the three men kept the law of purity best
whether the wounded man deserved the help he got
whether the innkeeper should be repaid his costs
which of the three proved a neighbour to the man
why: Luke 10:36–37: Jesus asks which of the three "was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves"; the lawyer says "he that shewed mercy on him," and Jesus says, "Go, and do thou likewise." The question turns from whom to help to how to be a neighbour.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (10:25–37), un experto en la ley le pregunta a Jesús: "¿Quién es mi prójimo?". Jesús responde con la parábola del buen samaritano. ¿Qué le pregunta Jesús al final?
options: cuál de los tres cumplió mejor la ley de pureza
si el herido merecía la ayuda que recibió
si al posadero había que pagarle sus gastos
cuál de los tres fue el prójimo de aquel hombre
es.why: Lucas 10:36–37: Jesús pregunta cuál de los tres "fue el prójimo del que cayó en manos de los ladrones"; el experto responde "el que tuvo compasión de él", y Jesús dice: "Ve y haz tú lo mismo". La pregunta pasa de a quién ayudar a cómo ser prójimo.

stem: In the Gospel of Luke (15), Jesus tells three parables in a row: the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son. According to Luke 15:1–2, what is he answering?
options: disciples arguing among themselves over who was the greatest
a rich ruler asking how to inherit eternal life
Pharisees and scribes grumbling that he eats with sinners
a crowd demanding a sign from heaven to prove him
why: Luke 15:1–3: tax collectors and sinners came near to hear him, and the Pharisees and scribes murmured, "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them"; then he spoke this parable to them. Each story ends in joy over what was lost and is found.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (15), Jesús cuenta tres parábolas seguidas: la oveja perdida, la moneda perdida y el hijo perdido. Según Lucas 15:1–2, ¿a qué está respondiendo?
options: a los discípulos que discuten entre sí quién de ellos es el mayor
a un hombre rico que pregunta cómo heredar la vida eterna
a fariseos y escribas que murmuran porque come con pecadores
a una multitud que le exige una señal del cielo como prueba
es.why: Lucas 15:1–3: los cobradores de impuestos y los pecadores se acercaban a escucharlo, y los fariseos y escribas murmuraban: "Este recibe a los pecadores y come con ellos"; entonces les contó esta parábola. Cada relato termina en alegría por lo que estaba perdido y se encuentra.

stem: In the Gospel of Luke (16:1–8), a manager about to lose his post cuts the debts owed to his master so the debtors will welcome him later. Why does Luke say the master commends him?
options: because he acted shrewdly to provide for his future
because he had repaid in full the goods he had wasted
because he had been honest about the true debts
because he gave the money he saved to the poor
why: Luke 16:8: "the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely" (shrewdly), adding that the children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light. He is praised for foresight, not honesty.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (16:1–8), un administrador a punto de perder su puesto rebaja las deudas que otros tienen con su amo para que después lo reciban. ¿Por qué dice Lucas que el amo lo elogia?
options: porque actuó con astucia para asegurar su futuro
porque devolvió por completo todo lo que había malgastado
porque fue honesto sobre las deudas reales
porque dio a los pobres el dinero que ahorró
es.why: Lucas 16:8: "el amo elogió al administrador injusto por haber actuado con astucia", y añade que los hijos de este mundo son más astutos con los suyos que los hijos de la luz. Se le alaba la previsión, no la honestidad.

stem: A family hosting a holiday dinner skips the usual round of relatives and well-off neighbours and instead seats people from the shelter down the street. Which teaching of Jesus in Luke 14 are they following?
options: choose the lowest seat at a feast rather than the place of honour
count the cost first, as a builder does before raising a tower
heal and do good on the Sabbath, as you'd pull an ox from a well
call the poor to your table, not those who can repay the favour
why: Luke 14:12–14: Jesus tells his host not to invite friends, kin or rich neighbours who will invite him back, but "call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind ... for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just." The lowest seat (14:7–11), the Sabbath healing (14:1–6) and counting the cost (14:28–30) are other teachings in the same chapter.

es.stem: Una familia que organiza una cena de fiesta deja de lado a los parientes y vecinos acomodados de siempre y, en cambio, sienta a su mesa a personas del albergue de la calle. ¿Qué enseñanza de Jesús en Lucas 14 está siguiendo?
options: elige el último lugar en un banquete y no el puesto de honor
calcula primero el costo, como quien va a levantar una torre
sana y haz el bien en sábado, como sacarías a un buey de un pozo
invita a tu mesa a los pobres, no a quienes te pueden devolver el favor
es.why: Lucas 14:12–14: Jesús le dice a su anfitrión que no invite a amigos, parientes ni vecinos ricos que lo inviten a su vez, sino "invita a los pobres, a los mancos, a los cojos y a los ciegos; y serás dichoso, porque ellos no te pueden corresponder; tu recompensa será en la resurrección de los justos". El último lugar (14:7–11), la curación en sábado (14:1–6) y calcular el costo (14:28–30) son otras enseñanzas del mismo capítulo.

stem: In the opening verses of the Gospel of Luke (1:1–4), what does Luke say about how he wrote his account, and why?
why: Luke 1:1–4: many have already written about these events; Luke draws on what was handed down by eyewitnesses and ministers of the word, has followed everything carefully from the start, and writes an orderly account for "most excellent Theophilus" so that he may know the certainty of what he has been taught.

rubric.point: Says he worked from what was handed down by eyewitnesses (and ministers of the word), or after carefully investigating everything from the beginning. Saying only 'he wrote it down' does not count.
Says his aim is that the reader may know the certainty or truth of what he was taught. 'To tell people about Jesus' counts as partly.
Mentions that it is addressed to Theophilus, that it is an orderly account, or that many others had already written (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En los primeros versículos del Evangelio de Lucas (1:1–4), ¿qué dice Lucas sobre cómo escribió su relato y para qué?
es.why: Lucas 1:1–4: muchos ya han escrito sobre estos hechos; Lucas se apoya en lo que transmitieron los testigos oculares y servidores de la palabra, lo ha investigado todo con cuidado desde el principio y escribe un relato ordenado para el "excelentísimo Teófilo", para que conozca la solidez de lo que se le ha enseñado.

stem: In the Gospel of Luke (24:13–35), two disciples walking to Emmaus meet the risen Jesus without knowing him. What does he explain to them on the road, and when do they recognize him?
why: Luke 24:27–35: "beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself"; at table in Emmaus he took bread, blessed it, broke it and gave it to them, and their eyes were opened. They tell the others he was known to them "in breaking of bread."

rubric.point: Says he explains the scriptures (Moses and the prophets) about himself, or why the Christ had to suffer. 'He talked about what had happened' without the scriptures counts as partly.
Says they recognize him at the meal, when he takes, blesses and breaks the bread. Saying only 'at dinner' counts as partly.
Mentions that he then vanishes, that their hearts burned within them on the road, that one is named Cleopas, or that they hurry back to Jerusalem (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Lucas (24:13–35), dos discípulos que caminan hacia Emaús se encuentran con Jesús resucitado sin reconocerlo. ¿Qué les explica en el camino y cuándo lo reconocen?
es.why: Lucas 24:27–35: "comenzando por Moisés y todos los profetas, les explicó lo que se refería a él en todas las Escrituras"; en la mesa, en Emaús, tomó el pan, lo bendijo, lo partió y se lo dio, y se les abrieron los ojos. Cuentan a los demás que lo reconocieron "al partir el pan".
